chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man whose nail breaks off: is it permissible for him to put gum upon it?

He عليه السلام said: “No. And he should not put upon it anything except what he is able to remove from it at the time of wudu (ablution), and he should not put upon it that to which the water does not reach.”

key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.عِلْكًا: gum or adhesive substance placed on the nail

ai.seo_question: Can a person put gum or a covering on a broken nail during wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a broken nail and what may be placed over it. It establishes that one must not apply a substance that prevents water from reaching the area during wudu (ablution), except something that can be removed at the time of purification.
